processRecommendations.process: Hobbing (rough) + Shaving/Grinding (finish) + CNC turning of blank
processRecommendations.reasoning: Solid steel gear, ISO 1328 class 7 with case-hardening requires hobbing to generate tooth form, carburise-quench heat treat, then form or profile grinding on OD/bore/tooth flanks to correct for heat-treat distortion. Bottom-up CNC estimate (0.817hr) covers blank machining/drilling but not gear-form generation or post-HT grind.

Drawing specifies case depth 0.6-0.9mm, 58-62 HRC — mandatory batch furnace carburising + quench + temper cycle, typically outsourced or run in-house batch furnace, not a per-part CNC cycle but adds cost/lead time.
ISO 1328 class 7 with case-hardened flanks (58-62 HRC) typically needs finish grinding after heat treat to correct distortion and hold quality class; adds a grinding operation on mach-grind.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Drawing states z=40 but B-rep geometry measures 38 teeth at r≈60mm tip circle — a mismatch of 2 teeth changes module/geometry relationship (mn=3mm assumes z=38 given OD=120mm). This is likely a drawing/geometry version mismatch or deliberate test case.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Confirm with design authority which is correct before cutting hob/tooling — do not proceed to hobbing until resolved; geometry (B-rep) value of 38 teeth is used per instruction to never contradict measured geometry.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Carburise+quench on a 120mm OD x 30mm face gear risks distortion affecting tooth quality class 7 conformance.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Plan for post-HT grinding allowance (0.05-0.1mm on flank) and pre-HT stress-relieve if required.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: A thread was detected in the geometry but not documented in the drawing's note block — could be a set-screw, oil hole, or unspecified feature.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Clarify thread spec (size, depth, class) with design office and add to drawing revision.

dfmIssues.description: Drawing calls out z=40 but the measured B-rep shows 38 teeth at the tip circle — a real geometric mismatch that will produce wrong hob selection or wrong center distance if not resolved.
dfmIssues.impact: Wrong tooling order or scrapped batch of 16,670 parts/month if unresolved before hobbing setup.
dfmIssues.fix: Reconcile drawing revision vs CAD model with design office before releasing to hobbing; use the measured 38-tooth geometry only once confirmed correct.

dfmIssues.description: Carburise + quench (58-62 HRC case) on a thin-web 30mm face gear can distort tooth profile/lead beyond class 7 tolerance without post-HT correction.
dfmIssues.impact: Rework or scrap if grinding step omitted; added ~15-20% cycle time and cost per part.
dfmIssues.fix: Add post-carburise profile/lead grind operation and pre-heat-treat stock allowance (~0.1-0.15mm per flank).

dfmIssues.description: 40mm H7 bore on a case-hardened part requires either protective masking during carburising or a bore grind/hone after heat treat to hold H7 after distortion.
dfmIssues.impact: Bore may close in or distort out of H7 tolerance post-HT, requiring a finish-bore operation.
dfmIssues.fix: Copper-plate or stop-off the bore before carburising, or add finish reaming/honing after heat treat.

dfmIssues.description: Geometry shows a threaded feature not called out on the drawing's spec table.
dfmIssues.impact: Ambiguous manufacturing intent could cause missed feature or incorrect thread spec during quoting.
dfmIssues.fix: Clarify thread location, size and class with the design office and update drawing.

dfmIssues.description: 3 machining setups identified (+X:39 faces, +Y:38 faces, +Z:2 faces) suggests gear needs re-fixturing for tooth generation vs face/bore ops.

analysis.aiExplanation: This is a 38-tooth (measured), module-3 external spur gear, 30mm face width, 40mm H7 bore, ISO 1328 class 7. Drawing specifies 20MnCr5 case-hardening steel, carburise + quench to 58-62 HRC with 0.6-0.9mm case depth, and 0° helix (confirmed spur). Note: the attached drawing states z=40 teeth, which conflicts with the B-rep measured tooth count of 38 — this is flagged as a critical discrepancy rather than silently resolved, per the measured-geometry precedence rule. Process route is hob-cut gear teeth on a turned steel blank, carburise + quench heat treat, then post-HT profile/lead grinding to hold class-7 tolerance given the distortion risk from case hardening. Material selection used the drawing's explicit MATERIAL and HEAT TREATMENT fields (20MnCr5, carburise+quench) rather than defaulting to aluminium, consistent with the dense drivetrain-component heuristic. Net weight (2.088kg) and blank cost use the steel density value from the OCCT weight table. Base CNC bottom-up cycle time (0.817hr) covers blank turning/drilling only; gear-specific hobbing and post-heat-treat grinding operations were added on top per gear-manufacturing best practice.
analysisLimitations: Tooth count discrepancy between drawing (z=40) and measured B-rep (z=38) could not be resolved automatically — flagged for engineering confirmation.
Exact grade 20MnCr5 (1.7147) is not in the valid materialId catalogue; mat-steel1045 used as nearest case-hardenable proxy, which may understate alloy/heat-treat cost premium.
Threaded feature detected in geometry has no corresponding drawing callout — its size/purpose is unconfirmed.
Case-hardening/grinding cycle times are rule-of-thumb estimates, not OCCT-derived; actual grind time depends on ground tooth flank stock removal, not modelled here.
Wall-thickness ray-cast unavailable, so heat-treat distortion risk assessment is qualitative only.

deterministicAnalysis.aiExplanation:
Derived deterministically for gear from the measured geometry. No AI call was made; every figure below is arithmetic on a measurement or a library lookup, and each states its own basis.

  • gear.teeth = 38 — counted 38 tip-circle patch(es) at r≈60.0 mm clustered to 38 angular positions [geometry, gear-teeth]
  • gear.helixAngleDeg = 0 — spur — 0° helix (assumed — confirm before quoting) [engineer, gear-helix]
  • gear.normalModuleMm = 3 — mn = tip Ø 120.0 / (z 38 + 2) = 3.00 mm — standard addendum; recon 120.0 mm vs measured OD 120.0 mm (assumed — confirm before quoting) [geometry, gear-module]
  • gear.faceWidthMm = 30 — axial span of the tip-land patches = 30.0 mm [geometry, gear-face]
  • gear.internal = false — tip patches face outward — external gear [geometry, gear-internal]
  • gear.qualityClass = 7 — ISO 1328 class 7 (assumed — confirm before quoting) [engineer, gear-quality]
  • gear.batchSize = 16670 — monthly delivery batches: 200,000/yr ÷ 12 [rule, gear-batch]

Still open (1):
  • What is the gear cut from? — The solid weighs the same in 20MnCr5 and 42CrMo4, so the CAD cannot tell a carburised gear from a through-hardened one — and the choice changes the heat-treat route, the finishing route and the feeds the teeth are cut at.

decisions.why: The solid weighs the same in 20MnCr5 and 42CrMo4, so the CAD cannot tell a carburised gear from a through-hardened one — and the choice changes the heat-treat route, the finishing route and the feeds the teeth are cut at. The model read "case_hardening_steel" off the drawing/context — confirm or correct it before it reaches the costing.
